title: Major shakeup for RuPaul's Drag Race UK
standfirst: The BBC has dropped Drag Race UK after eight seasons — here's what changes for viewers, what happens to the cash prize, and what a first-ever UK All Stars could look like.

body.text: On September 9th 2026, it was announced that RuPaul's Drag Race UK and RuPaul's Drag Race UK vs The World have been dropped by the BBC. The BBC acted as its broadcaster from 2019 to 2026, with 8 seasons of the main Drag Race UK, and 3 seasons of the spin-off, UK vs The World. The BBC has now handed over all rights to its main production company, World Of Wonder. The BBC stated they made this decision as part of their plan to make £500m in savings, also stating it was facing "very difficult choices" in the face of "significant financial pressures". All 11 seasons of the show are set to join WOW Presents Plus following the finale of the currently airing 8th season. It has also been confirmed that the current seasons will still be available on BBC iPlayer once the move is complete, although new seasons produced solely by World Of Wonder will not join the iPlayer.
So what does this mean for you, the viewer?

Future seasons of RuPaul's Drag Race UK will continue production under World Of Wonder (WOW) and will be available to stream on WOW Presents Plus. For UK viewers this now means you will need to pay to watch upcoming seasons of Drag Race UK. WOW Presents Plus costs £4.99 per month, or £49.99 per year. Many viewers may already be subscribed to this platform as it is the main way to watch international seasons in the UK.

Shortly after the BBC dropped Drag Race UK, World Of Wonder announced on Instagram that a brand new spin-off, RuPaul's Drag Race UK All Stars would be premiering in Autumn 2027. After many years of the audience requesting, WOW has finally delivered a UK installment of Drag Race All Stars, and the public couldn't be more excited.

body.text: What should you expect to see now that the BBC's broadcasting rules no longer apply?

In earlier seasons, the BBC did not allow the winner of the show to receive a cash prize, although in more recent seasons a small cash prize of £25,000 was believed to be allowed due to a workaround in the BBC's restrictions. Now that Drag Race UK is no longer held under these restrictions, you can potentially expect a much larger cash prize. While there is no confirmed amount, other franchises typically offer a lot more such as Canada's Drag Race awards $100,000 CAD to the winner or the main US franchise awards $200,000 USD. Given Drag Race UK was historically under heavy restrictions, it's reasonable to believe that an increase may be an option.

We can also expect changes to the Drag Race UK set, possibly including a new 'Werk Room' and a brand new main stage. Given World Of Wonder has always been responsible for the show's set design, it wouldn't be a huge surprise to see a new set for the first edition of All Stars. It's possible that World Of Wonder wants to highlight a 'new era' for Drag Race UK and the transition from the BBC and WOW Presents Plus.
So, is this the future of Drag Race UK?

It is entirely possible for WOW to keep hold of the show, as having full control is convenient for them. But a shift to a new broadcaster such as ITV or Channel 4 isn't off the table, as UK vs The World season 1 champion Blu Hydrangea hoped for in a social media post. Whatever happens next, RuPaul's Drag Race UK's biggest shakeup in herstory is officially under way.
